response.sql: SELECT store_id, AVG(total_amount) AS avg_rental_sum, AVG(payment_count) AS avg_rental_payment_count FROM (SELECT r.rental_id, i.store_id, SUM(p.amount) AS total_amount, COUNT(*) AS payment_count FROM payment p JOIN rental r ON r.rental_id = p.rental_id JOIN inventory i ON i.inventory_id = r.inventory_id WHERE p.amount >= 4.99 GROUP BY r.rental_id, i.store_id) t GROUP BY store_id

assumptions.assumption: The 4.99 cutoff is inclusive: payments with amount >= 4.99 are kept (4.99 is a common amount in this data, so inclusive vs. exclusive changes the result).

Inner joins from payment to rental to inventory drop payments with a NULL rental_id or with no matching rental/inventory row. The store ID is the inventory item's store, not the customer's or staff member's.
Per-rental figures are computed first (one row per rental ID and inventory store ID), then averaged per store. Each rental counts once, not each payment.

alternatives.interpretation: The cutoff is exclusive: keep only payments with amount strictly greater than 4.99.
